- Teeth and inner mouth: at frame 48 the teeth are a blurry grey patch in all four columns, including BEFORE, so this is a baseline artefact and not a regression. Enlarged, r3's patch has slightly different grey/white patterning (the diff panel shows coloured blotches on the teeth), but I would not notice it at normal size. At frame 184 (widest mouth) the upper teeth row, tongue and lip edges look the same in all four. Raw mouth-crop diff there: r2 max 2, r3 mean 1.25 / max 18, r4 mean 0.61 / max 9 LSB.
- Lip edges: frame 146 is r4's most different frame. Its diff panel shows a bright band along the lip parting line and teeth (max 53 LSB). Even at 4x side by side I cannot reliably see a change in the lip line or teeth; at most a slight difference in the dark parting line near the left mouth corner, and I am not confident of that.
- Beard/stubble: not applicable, this identity has no facial hair. Skin texture around the mouth and chin looks the same in every column.
- Chin line and jaw: the jaw contour looks identical in all columns. The r3 diff panel, and more faintly r4's, shows a thin curve along the lower-right jaw/neck edge (frames 1, 144, 146, 240). In that region r3 has mean 1.82 / max 49 LSB and r4 has 0.69 / max 24. It is not visible in the composited frame.
- Seam: no visible seam change between columns. At frame 240 there is a faint vertical tone step on the nose and lower-lip midline (about x=215 in the zoom cell) in all four columns, BEFORE included, so no round introduced it.
- Colour: at canvas scale my first impression was that the r2/r3 full-frame faces looked slightly lighter than BEFORE. Measurement does not support this. Full-frame MAD vs BEFORE is about 1.2 LSB for every round (codec noise), and the quality tool's Lab deltaE of mean face colour is 0.005 / 0.033 / 0.004.

Overall: the differences are only visible in the x8 diff panels. r2 is effectively identical to BEFORE. r3 changes texture everywhere by small amounts. r4 concentrates its change on the lip opening, with occasional spikes (frame 146).

problems.description: The overlay shows metric values but not pass/fail. All three quality JSONs have verdict FAIL. The strict chin.landmark_dev_mean_px <= 0.05 gate fails for r2 (0.0502, over by 0.0002), r3 (0.255) and r4 (0.141). chin.landmark_dev_p99_px <= 0.15 fails for r3 (0.78) and r4 (0.555). Under the proposed calibrated gate (report-only: mean <= 0.1, p99 <= 0.35), r2 would pass and r3 and r4 would not. A viewer sees 'r4 NEW' highlighted in yellow with no sign that it misses the jaw+lip landmark gates.

verified_facts: Method: CPU only, no GPU jobs. I wrote a streaming check (/tmp/claude-0/-workspace/866169db-0af2-4cde-9a98-79a398efeda7/scratchpad/verify_lineage/verify.py and diffcell.py; results in v_<id>.json there). It decodes one frame at a time and rebuilds every column's raw refined composite with chin.py fd753e7d... from one shared decode of source.mp4.

BEFORE is the pre-change render and matches bit for bit. For all 6 identities, every artifact sha in render.json (faces.npz, generated_landmarks.npy, chin_delta.npy, refined_raw.mp4, pixel_checks.json, mask_samples.npz) matches the file on disk. render.json records UNet 'TensorRT FP16 batch8' (unet_trt.ts 2c1a9338...), compiled TAESD, chin_strength 1.0 and chin.py fd753e7d.... My independent rebuild reproduces render.json raw_refined_sha256 6/6.

The rounds also match bit for bit. My rebuild reproduces every recorded raw_refined_sha256 for r2/r3/r4 (18/18, every clip in the V_* capture JSONs). chin_delta recomputed with chin.prepare equals the saved one 24/24. lineage_report.json's claims are therefore correct.

All columns share the same inputs. chin.py (fd753e7d...) and blending.py (6e5de1bf...) are identical in /workspace/MuseTalk and MuseTalk-perf300, and the harness code_integrity says matches_accepted_render_json=True. The harness loads latents, audio features, boxes and cropboxes from each accepted identity's cache.pt, so every column uses the same source frames and audio features. Video audio is that identity's speech.wav (24 kHz mono, 10.0 s) encoded to AAC.

The fps labels trace to measured runs. r2 350.2 = Te_srcmix_taesdtrt_n6 [350.7, 349.7]; r3 415.6 = Tf_srcv1_taesdtrt_n6 [416.6, 414.7]; r4 414.9 = T_srcblkA8 [415.6, 414.1]. Each timed T* run and its V* video capture run have identical effective env, engine dir, harness code and per-identity raw_refined hashes, so the video shows exactly the frames that were timed. The Q* quality runs have the same hashes, and the faces.npz files are byte-identical.
The cyan metric lines describe the exact pixels on screen. The quality tool's A and B composite shas equal the video's BEFORE and round column shas (36/36).

BEFORE's '148-171 fps' is accurate but single-stream: render.json warm_render_fps 148.0-170.6, one warm run each. Per-frame tracking IPC (754-780 ms) plus compose (557-761 ms) take about 94% of the 1.41-1.62 s render. The harness serial baseline (S_serial_baseline) gives median 164.8 fps (146.2-186.8).

The same 6-stream harness measured the unchanged BEFORE pipeline at 251.8 fps aggregate (Ta_baseline_n6: 252.0 / 251.6). All 144/144 clips there match the accepted raw and faces hashes, GPU busy fraction was 0.999 at 3.97 ms/frame, and gateE_baseline_n6_loops1 agrees at 252.4. This figure appears only in the JSON and logs (seq_A.out), not in any video label or the READMEs checked.

Every column goes through the same single encode. There is one libx264 encode per identity: crf=14.0 (read from the x264 SEI), yuv420p, 24 fps, 240 frames, 10.0 s, 1600 px wide and 1608-1612 px tall. Each column's full-frame row is equally faithful to its own raw composite (39.50-39.89 dB, differences between columns at most 0.02 dB), and so is the mouth zoom (40.42-41.05 dB luma), so no column gets an encoding advantage.
Frame alignment is identical: each column matches its raw frame at the same index. At lag 0 it scores 39.5-39.9 dB; at lag -1 or +1 it drops to 33.1-35.6 dB, for every column and identity.

The x8 diff is computed the same way for every round column: clip(|face_k - face_BEFORE| * 8), nearest-neighbour 256 to 400 px. The encoded r4 panel matches my recomputation up to encoding noise (MSE 5.8-8.1). Every column uses the same mouth crop, taken from BEFORE's landmarks.
The source-prefix cache used by r2-r4 is precomputed per identity before the timed loop (gpu.py GpuIssuer init). That is a per-avatar precompute like cache.pt, which BEFORE's fps also excludes.

The older A/B videos were biased toward the candidate. A (stored refined_raw.mp4) is x264 crf 18 at 1.51-1.91 Mbit/s; B (the V_* captures) is crf 12 at 4.94-5.80 Mbit/s, 2.9-3.3x the bitrate. Both are then re-encoded at crf 12. Measured against the raw composites in the r4 A/B videos, B is 0.56-0.78 dB closer to its raw frames than A over the full frame and 0.73-1.22 dB closer in the mouth (luma). On their own, the stored accepted mp4 scores 38.87-40.15 dB in the mouth (luma) against 40.37-41.10 dB for the r4 crf-12 capture. I measured only the r4 A/B set; the r2 and r3 sets use the same kinds of input (crf 18 vs crf 12, checked with ffprobe), so the same bias direction is expected but was not measured.

problems.description: The fps labels compare different measurement modes, which is unfair to BEFORE. BEFORE is labelled 'single-stream 148-171 fps' (one warm serial run, mostly CPU tracking and compose), while the rounds show 6-stream aggregate numbers. The same harness ran the unchanged, bit-exact BEFORE pipeline at 251.8 fps aggregate over 6 streams (Ta_baseline_n6). The video suggests gains of 2.0-2.8x; like-for-like, the gains are 1.39x (r2), 1.65x (r3) and 1.65x (r4). Uncertain: Ta ran at 06:44 UTC, about 12-15 h before the round runs, with less free host RAM (5.6 GB minimum versus about 9-10 GB), and the JSON does not record whether other processes were using the GPU. Contention could have understated the baseline, but I cannot confirm it.
problems.suggested_fix: Relabel BEFORE as '251.8 fps aggregate (6 streams, same harness; serial render loop 148-171)'. Add each round's speedup over 251.8 to its label. Change the same sentence in the r2 README ('The before-point is the accepted single-stream render loop'). Ideally re-run Ta_baseline_n6 right before or after T_srcblkA8 once the GPU is free, to rule out contention.

problems.description: The video leaves out the quality verdicts and thresholds, which flatters the new rounds. The cyan lines give bare numbers. Quality tool verdicts: r2 passes 2/6 identities (the strict landmark gate fails on 4/6; the calibrated 0.10/0.35 bar passes 5/6, with the full-beard identity at p99 0.475). r3 fails 6/6. r4 fails 6/6 on the strict bar (0.05/0.15 px) and also on the calibrated bar (mean 0.105-0.171, p99 0.37-0.65). The r4 README also records the UNet latent max_abs of 1.28 failing its 0.5 gate. The TRT TAESD used by r2-r4 has decoder_trt_gate verdict FAIL (max 5 LSB against a limit of 3). The older A/B overlay printed 'verdict FAIL'; the lineage overlay and the lineage README table dropped it, and the README frames r4 only against '±1 LSB noise'. The README's numeric ranges themselves are correct (I recomputed them from the JSONs).
problems.suggested_fix: Add a line under each round column such as 'quality tool: FAIL, landmarks 0.171/0.59 px vs 0.05/0.15 strict, 0.10/0.35 calibrated', and show the limits next to the lip, flicker and chin values. Add a verdict column (PASS count out of 6) and the UNet and TAESD gate results to the lineage README table.

problems.description: The diff panel caption 'black = identical' is not true after the crf-14 yuv420p encode. I checked 3 identities, every 8th frame. Of the face pixels that differ by at least 1 LSB, only 26-36% (r2), 47-59% (r4) and 80-88% (r3) still show at least 4/255 in the encoded panel. Most of r2's changed pixels and about half of r4's show as black. This applies to every round equally but understates how much of the face changed. Also, the video's own coding error (about 39.5-41 dB against raw) is larger than the actual r4-vs-BEFORE mouth difference (47.7-50.1 dB PSNR). The full-frame and zoom rows are fair, but they cannot show changes that small.
problems.suggested_fix: Encode the diff panel losslessly (a separate yuv444p crf 0 or ffv1 file, or PNG stills), or give any non-zero difference a visible floor or a colormap. Change the caption to 'black = < ~1-2 LSB after encoding' and point to the raw numbers.

problems.description: The '3x mouth zoom' label is wrong. The actual factor is 1.75x-2.53x per identity (mouth box 158-228 px wide scaled into a 400 px column; black_woman is 1.75x), and the non-integer nearest-neighbour scaling duplicates pixels unevenly. The full-frame row is a 0.78x INTER_AREA downscale, so beard, cheek and jaw detail outside the mouth box is only ever seen downscaled. The diff panel covers only the 256 px generated face; composite changes from the chin warp outside the face box are never shown (0.6-2.2% of changed pixel-frames; max 2-6 LSB for r4 and up to 15 for r3). All of this applies equally to every column.
problems.suggested_fix: Print the computed zoom factor, or use an integer 3x crop (for example 133 px into 400). Render with --col-width 512 for a native full frame, and add a 1:1 or 2x jaw-and-beard crop, or a composite-level diff panel alongside the face-only one.
